identity.real_world_identity_notes: Reiza's renamed Ferrari 360 GT, the GT2 car of the same period, carried in AMS2 as Milano GT36. The record previously said no real-world analogue had been established; the maintainer identified it, in the same renaming that makes Milano 55 GT1 the Prodrive 550 Maranello. No source for the 360 GT's transmission has been consulted, so unlike its GT1 stablemate nothing here is corroborated: the six sequential gears and the automatic cut are the drive's, and whether the real car needs the clutch to go down a gear is not established. The 550 requires it, but that is a different car and is not inherited.

wheel_rim.notes: Direct cockpit inspection showed a round rim without an integrated display; exact diameter remains unknown.

notes: With Auto Clutch disabled, the car stalled when moving from rest without physical clutch input.
All six sequential-stick gears accepted clutch-free full-throttle upshifts with automatic throttle cut.
Clutch-free downshifts were accepted and no automatic throttle blip was observed; authentic rev matching therefore requires the driver to blip the throttle manually.
No unconfirmed real-world analogue is used to infer controls.
Live-tested in AMS2 1.6.9.91 with Auto Clutch disabled.
Standing-start clutch, six-speed sequential stick without paddles, automatic cut, no automatic blip, and round no-display rim were directly observed.

confidence.basis: Exact simulator identity, modeled cockpit hardware, and all material shift behavior were directly tested; no unconfirmed real-world identity is asserted.

claims.basis: Official release context and exact live CarModel/class observation establish the fictional simulated identity.
Direct current-game tests and cockpit inspection establish six-speed sequential-stick hardware, start clutch, automatic cut, absence of automatic blip, required manual rev matching, and wheel shape.
